title: Turn a rubric into judge predictions
purpose: Enable a learner to convert the explicit regression criterion and labeled cases from EP-01 into auditable binary judge predictions using a bounded rubric, cached offline responses, strict parsing, stable case alignment, and disagreement inspection.
prerequisites: The learner can read and edit basic Python and run Jupyter notebook cells.
The learner understands from EP-01 that human_label = 1 means the defined regression is present and human_label = 0 means it is absent.
build/lesson-01/eval_cases.jsonl exists and contains the approved case_id, input, candidate_output, and human_label fields.

user_stories.title: Bound the judge with one rubric
user_stories.statement: As an AI feature owner, I want a rubric that translates the existing regression criterion into explicit verdict rules so that the judge evaluates the intended failure instead of unrelated output quality.
user_stories.one_idea: An LLM judge needs a bounded rubric with the decision criterion, positive-class mapping, permitted evidence, and exclusions stated explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: The rubric preserves the EP-01 decision boundary and maps regression present to judge_label 1 and regression absent to judge_label 0.
The rubric tells the judge to use only the stored input and candidate_output and to ignore unrelated qualities such as tone or polish.
The section distinguishes the human label used as reference from the judge prediction and prevents human_label from being included in the judge request.

user_stories.title: Make responses replayable
user_stories.statement: As an eval maintainer, I want each judge response to follow a small response contract and be cached by case ID so that the evaluation can be rerun offline and audited without another paid call.
user_stories.one_idea: A versioned rubric plus a strict, cached response contract turns an otherwise variable model interaction into a reproducible evaluation input.
acceptance_criteria: Each cached response is keyed by a stable case_id and contains exactly one binary verdict plus a brief evidence-based reason.
The lesson explains that cached responses demonstrate the grading pipeline but do not measure live-provider variance.
The offline path requires no API key, network access, model weights, or paid call.

user_stories.title: Parse and align predictions
user_stories.statement: As an eval maintainer, I want strict parsing and one-to-one case alignment so that malformed, missing, duplicate, or unknown responses fail before they become grader inputs.
user_stories.one_idea: Judge output becomes usable evaluation data only after its verdict is validated and joined to ground truth by stable identity rather than row order.
acceptance_criteria: Parsing accepts only the declared binary verdict values and rejects missing or malformed verdicts with an actionable case_id-specific error.
Alignment proves exactly one response for every evaluation case, no duplicate case IDs, and no unknown or missing IDs.
The produced prediction records preserve case_id and human_label unchanged and add judge_label and judge_reason without computing aggregate metrics.

user_stories.title: Inspect disagreements before scoring
user_stories.statement: As an evaluator, I want to compare each judge prediction with the human label so that disagreements remain inspectable evidence rather than disappearing inside an aggregate score.
user_stories.one_idea: A human-judge disagreement is a review target, not automatic proof that either side is correct.

checkpoints.capability: Run an offline LLM-as-judge rubric over the evaluation set and inspect disagreements against human labels.
checkpoints.observable_check: After completing US-L02-01 through US-L02-04, a fresh-kernel notebook run loads all EP-01 cases, replays one cached response per case, validates and aligns every prediction by case_id, prints a disagreement table containing case_id, human_label, judge_label, and judge_reason, writes judge_predictions.jsonl, and ends with PASS.

acceptance_criteria: The learner can identify each disagreement by case_id and inspect both labels plus the judge's stated reason.
The section warns against silently treating the judge as ground truth or changing human labels to improve apparent agreement.
The lesson stops at record-level inspection and explicitly defers confusion-matrix counts, precision, and recall to EP-03.

visible_checks: Load eval_cases.jsonl and print the case count plus the invariant label mapping inherited from EP-01.
Render the bounded rubric for one case and prove that the judge request contains input and candidate_output but not human_label.
Load cached judge responses and validate allowed verdicts, non-empty reasons, unique case IDs, and exact case-ID coverage; print actionable errors or PASS.
Convert verdicts to binary judge_label values, align them to cases by case_id, and prove that case_id and human_label are unchanged.

Print the disagreement rows with case_id, human_label, judge_label, and judge_reason; write and reload judge_predictions.jsonl, compare it with the in-memory records, and print the output path plus a final PASS.
build_along.offline_replay: The canonical Jupyter notebook uses Python 3.12 and repository-contained eval cases plus cached judge responses. From a fresh kernel it renders requests, parses cached responses, validates exact case-ID coverage, writes and reloads judge_predictions.jsonl, and displays disagreements without network access, API keys, model weights, or paid calls. The executed notebook and actual output are recorded under output/lesson-02/.

capstone_trace: CONTEXT.md breaking point 2 identifies the learner failure addressed by this epic: an authoritative-sounding model judge can apply an underspecified rubric inconsistently or import irrelevant preferences. US-L02-01 bounds that rubric, and CP-L02-03-A makes the complete response observable through validated offline predictions and disagreement inspection.
CP-L02-03-A supplies the capstone's validated judge-prediction layer: each EP-01 case receives one parsed binary prediction and an inspectable reason through offline replay.
The bounded rubric preserves the course invariant that label 1 means regression present, so EP-03 can compare judge_label with human_label without reversing the positive class.

build/lesson-02/judge_predictions.jsonl is useful alone as a case-level disagreement report and is the required EP-03 prediction input; each record contains case_id, unchanged human_label, judge_label, and judge_reason.

Exact ID coverage, uniqueness, strict verdict parsing, invariant checks, and round-trip persistence prevent EP-03 from scoring reordered, missing, duplicated, malformed, or semantically reversed predictions.

This lesson satisfies the second part of the capstone contract. EP-03 must independently join eval_cases.jsonl and judge_predictions.jsonl by case_id, validate human-label agreement across the artifacts, compute TP/FP/FN/TN, print precision and recall with zero-division handling, persist grader_report.json, and prove known expected values.

Searcher brief: research only EP-02 claims needed to define bounded rubric design, distinguish reference labels from judge predictions, support structured-output validation and stable-ID alignment, characterize limitations of cached offline replay, and interpret disagreement as a review target; write only agent/evals-course-factory/output/lesson-02/searcher/sources.json. Do not research or draft EP-03 formulas, metrics, lesson prose, notebook code, or live-provider integrations.

Builder brief: consume only this approved plan, approved EP-02 research, and build/lesson-01/eval_cases.jsonl; write exactly course/lesson-02.md plus the notebook, cached-response fixture, and persisted learner artifact under build/lesson-02/, with actual executed results only under output/lesson-02/. Preserve four text-only, one-idea sections of 300-500 words and about 2-3 minutes each, followed by exactly one incremental build-along of at most 20 minutes. Use an editable Jupyter notebook that runs offline top-to-bottom from a fresh kernel on Python 3.12, prints every declared visible check, preserves case_id and human_label semantics, and persists judge_predictions.jsonl. Do not use Mermaid, raster images, quizzes, flashcards, video, audio, paid calls, model weights, live-provider integration, or EP-03 metric computation.
